title: ViBe: Background as a Bag of Samples

pages.h1: The background is a bag of pixels you’ve already seen
pages.lead: ViBe throws away the statistics. Each pixel remembers twenty raw values it has been in the past, and a new value is background if it lands close to a couple of them. No Gaussians, no histograms, no learning rate — and it runs faster than everything it replaced.

pages.h1: Forgetting at random is the whole trick
pages.lead: The sample model is simple enough to fit on a napkin. What makes ViBe work is how the samples get replaced: conservatively, randomly, sub-sampled in time, and — the strange one — leaking sideways into the neighbours.

pages.h1: Parameters, failure modes, and what came after
pages.lead: Where the four knobs actually matter, the six ways ViBe fails on real footage, how ViBe+ and PBAS patched it, and the patent you should know about before shipping.
